summary: Duplicate useEffect causes double subscription to BlockNote editor changes, leading to duplicate content processing and state corruption
failure_scenario: User types in editor → handleEditorChange is called twice → setContent and evaluate each fire twice → state becomes inconsistent, evaluations run twice, potential duplicate network calls

summary: fetch function passed to useAssistant is recreated on every render without memoization, risking reset of assistant message history and state
failure_scenario: User types a message → component re-renders → new fetch function created → useAssistant detects change and resets internal state → previous conversation history is lost

summary: Timer expiration calls onDismiss without checking if parent is mounted, risking React state update on unmounted component warning
failure_scenario: User leaves page while interruption timer is counting down → timer reaches 0 → onDismiss is called → parent component may have unmounted → React warning: Can't call setState on an unmounted component

summary: Overlay remains clickable during opacity fade-out transition because pointer-events are not disabled, causing re-opening on click
failure_scenario: User clicks 'Passer' or closes interruption → opacity-0 applied but overlay still in DOM → user accidentally clicks overlay during transition → bubble re-opens unexpectedly

summary: "leech" mastery status incorrectly mapped to "forge" badge variant, displaying wrong visual feedback for weakest mastery level
failure_scenario: Student concept has status 'leech' → displays 'forge' badge (typically green/complete) instead of a warning variant → user incorrectly perceives concept as mastered when it's actually weak

summary: Duplicate case statement for 'à revoir' (lines 24-25) and likely typo 'àrevoyer' (line 27) that will never match valid input
failure_scenario: Code is confusing to maintainers; 'àrevoyer' typo is dead code that should be removed; duplicate case suggests copy-paste error

summary: Mock confidence value uses Math.random() producing unpredictable scores between 70-90, not reflecting actual AI confidence
failure_scenario: Every AI response shows a different random confidence score (e.g., 73%, then 88%, then 71%) → misleading user about system's actual certainty

summary: Flame icon uses absolute positioning with transforms when flex centering on parent would suffice, adding unnecessary complexity
failure_scenario: If parent flex layout changes, absolute positioning may misalign the icon; harder to maintain than pure flex solution
